jukan-intel-14a-2028-ramp:
Intel confirmed on its Q2 2026 earnings call, reported July 23, that it made an internal decision during the quarter to move its next-generation 14A chip process to full high-volume production in 2028, semiconductor analyst Jukan reports.

## The quote itself
14A is Intel's most advanced upcoming manufacturing node, built using high-NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, the cutting edge of chipmaking equipment. On the call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said: 'We remain on track for 14A risk production for our internal products in second half of 2027, and we made the decision in Q2 to fully commit to high volume ramp in 2028.'

@@REF@@Earnings call transcript: Intel tops Q2 2026 estimates as shares rebound after hours (Investing.com, 2026-07-23)|https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-intel-tops-q2-2026-estimates-as-shares-rebound-after-hours-93CH-4810201

## A year ahead of what the market expected
Jukan notes Wall Street had generally assumed 14A wouldn't reach high-volume production until 2029, so this amounts to Intel confirming a timeline roughly a year ahead of what the market had priced in, per press and analyst commentary rather than a direct Intel comparison to a specific 2029 figure.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Tesla-NVIDIA_GPU_cluster_%283706444821%29.jpg/960px-Tesla-NVIDIA_GPU_cluster_%283706444821%29.jpg|Whether Intel can win business like this, high-performance chip racks built at scale, from a truly competitive advanced node is the bigger question behind the 14A timeline.|Wikimedia Commons|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tesla-NVIDIA_GPU_cluster_(3706444821).jpg

## Riding a blowout quarter
The update follows Intel's Q2 results: revenue of $16.1 billion, up 25% year over year, its fastest growth in roughly 15 years, driven by data center and AI product revenue that jumped 59% to $6.3 billion.

@@REF@@Intel's stock jumps as chipmaker rides AI boom to fastest revenue growth in almost 15 years (CNBC, 2026-07-23)|https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/07/23/intel-intc-earnings-report-q2-2026.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108315138-17804039612026-06-02t070118z_913331550_rc2jllarvolb_rtrmadp_0_computex-intel.jpeg?v=1780403995

## A roadmap promise, or proof Intel Foundry can compete
As of this report, 14A still has no confirmed external foundry customers, the 2028 target covers only Intel's own products. Whether Intel actually hits risk production for internal chips in the second half of 2027, the next real checkpoint, will start to show whether this reaffirmed schedule is Intel Foundry rebuilding credibility or just another roadmap promise that means little until proven with real yields and paying customers.
kobeissi-trump-massive-iran-attack:
President Trump told Axios in an exclusive interview he is close to deciding on what he called a massive attack on Iran, saying 'we are all set for it' and that the strike would be 'bigger than ever before,' quotes independently confirmed by Forbes, The Hill, CNBC, and other outlets.

## What Trump actually said
He added that Israel 'would join in two minutes' if he asked them to, but that the US 'doesn't need anybody else' to act. Trump said the Houthis, Iran's proxy in Yemen, 'haven't received enough pain yet,' a reference to their recent strikes on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.

@@REF@@Exclusive: Trump 'close' to decision on 'massive attack' on Iran (Axios, 2026-07-23)|https://www.axios.com/2026/07/23/trump-axios-iran-interview|https://images.axios.com/njGu3UhG7vDYQ_1F5zDSHCQfOTo=/0x0:4662x2622/1366x768/2026/07/23/1784820087552.jpeg

## Weeks of escalation, and markets pricing it in
The comments come after weeks of escalating rhetoric since a ceasefire collapsed and fighting resumed in early July, and after Trump's own social media posts warning that any damage to ships or cargo will be paid for out of frozen Iranian funds. Brent crude broke above $100 a barrel this week and the 10-year Treasury yield pushed past 4.70%, its highest since January 2025, moves that CNBC and other outlets tie to oil-driven inflation fears from the conflict.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg/960px-NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg|Oil above $100 and yields at 2026 highs are the kind of moves that show up on trading floors like this.|Wikimedia Commons|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg

## The $900 billion figure doesn't hold up
The original post tying this to a one-day $900 billion Nasdaq loss doesn't match the closest verified figure: Bloomberg reported the 'Magnificent Seven' megacap stocks lost $797 billion in a single session around the same time, and that selloff was attributed primarily to AI-capex and earnings jitters following Alphabet and Tesla's results, with Iran tensions cited as a secondary, compounding factor rather than the main cause.

@@REF@@Magnificent 7 Lose $797 Billion as AI Skeptics Dump Tech Stocks (Bloomberg, 2026-07-23)|https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-23/magnificent-7-loses-767-billion-as-ai-skeptics-dump-tech-stocks

## Rhetoric before, action this time
Trump has hinted at a massive attack on Iran for weeks without following through immediately. If he follows through on a strike he himself calls bigger than ever before, oil, shipping routes through Hormuz, and risk assets broadly would likely see another sharp move. But similar warnings from Trump have not always turned into immediate action, so whether this is the moment rhetoric becomes reality, or another escalation warning that fades, is still open.
jukan-nvidia-800v-hvdc-delay:
Nvidia's next-generation 800 volt HVDC power system, a way of delivering electricity inside AI server racks that cuts energy loss and lets racks scale to higher power levels, may not reach large-scale production until 2028 or later, a year later than the 2027 timeline the market had expected, according to research firm SemiAnalysis.

## Why power, not chip speed, is the bottleneck now
HVDC, short for high-voltage direct current, replaces the many small power converters inside a server rack with fewer, more efficient ones. That matters because AI racks are increasingly limited by how much power and cooling they can pack in, not by chip performance.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Datacenter_Server_Racks_%2822370909788%29.jpg/960px-Datacenter_Server_Racks_%2822370909788%29.jpg|This is the kind of rack infrastructure the 800V HVDC system is meant to power.|Wikimedia Commons|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Datacenter_Server_Racks_(22370909788).jpg

## Two different reads on the same delay
SemiAnalysis's own reporting has pointed to hyperscalers favoring a more mature low-voltage transition over immediate 800V adoption, alongside related delays in co-packaged optics for Nvidia's Rubin Ultra platform, as part of the story. Semiconductor analyst Jukan, citing supply chain sources, argues the market has misread the delay differently: the issue is a validation problem with first-generation product designs, not a change to Nvidia's technology roadmap. Power cabinets, battery backup units, and battery packs have all been resubmitted for validation testing, these sources say, a normal part of qualifying new hardware.

@@CMP@@SemiAnalysis's read|Hyperscalers are holding back on 800V adoption itself, alongside related packaging delays, pushing the real ramp to 2028|Jukan's supply-chain sources|The roadmap hasn't changed. First-gen hardware just needs to be revalidated, and volume production is still coming in 1Q 2027

## Delta Electronics is said to be ready
Taiwan's Delta Electronics, a major supplier of data center power systems, battery backup units, and energy-management platforms for this architecture, is described as positioned for a ramp once validation clears.

@@REF@@NVIDIA, Google Among First 800V HVDC Adopters (TrendForce, 2026-06-15)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/06/15/news-nvidia-google-may-be-first-to-adopt-800v-hvdc-initial-3q26-shipments-may-boost-delta-and-infrastructure-suppliers/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/15144210/NVIDIA-800V-HVDC-20260615-624x351.jpg

## What's actually riding on this
The system is meant to support Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin chip platform, and any slip in power hardware readiness could delay how fast data centers can deploy Rubin at scale, even if the chips themselves ship on time. Whether the real culprit is hyperscaler caution or first-gen validation delays matters less to data center operators than the bottom line: how much power they can actually plug in, and when.
jukan-korea-leverage-deposit-hike:
South Korean regulators have moved up the effective date for tighter rules on single-stock leverage products, tied to stocks like Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, to July 31, about five days earlier than the original August 5 plan, semiconductor analyst Jukan reports.

## What's actually changing
The core change raises the basic deposit required to trade these products from 10 million won to 30 million won, and requires that deposit to be in cash only, stocks, bonds, and other securities will no longer count toward it. This applies to both new and existing positions each time a buy order is placed.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg/960px-NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg|Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, the two stocks these leverage products track, trade on a floor like this.|Wikimedia Commons|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg

## A separate rule stays on its original date
A related rule tightening how closely leveraged products must track their underlying index was also floated for early implementation, but reporting on the actual regulatory announcement indicates that piece remains scheduled for August 19 as originally planned, only the deposit hike itself, and possibly a minimum-order-unit change under separate review, moved up.

@@REF@@삼전닉스 레버리지 예탁금 3000만원으로…31일부터 조기시행 (디지털타임스, 2026-07-24)|https://www.dt.co.kr/article/12074504|https://wimg.dt.co.kr/news/cms/2026/07/24/rcv.YNA.20260723.PYH2026072317130001300_R.jpg

## Five days early, and critics call that thin
The move follows South Korean President Lee Jae-myung's public call for authorities to prepare countermeasures quickly and act boldly after leverage-fueled swings in semiconductor stocks. Industry critics quoted in Korean financial press say shaving five days off the start date barely qualifies as bold, and call it a rushed response without proper consultation.

@@REF@@이 대통령, 삼전·닉스 레버리지 ETF에 '보완대책 신속히 마련하라' (파이낸셜뉴스, 2026-07-15)|https://www.fnnews.com/news/202607151500047401|https://image.fnnews.com/resource/media/image/2026/07/15/202607151054378360_l.jpg

## Who actually feels the deposit hike
Whether foreign investors and institutions face the same 30 million won requirement isn't spelled out in the coverage reviewed here, so that specific carve-out claim can't be confirmed. What is clear is that tripling the cash deposit to 30 million won mechanically raises the bar mainly for smaller retail traders, since well-capitalized individual investors can meet that threshold without much strain, while the products themselves, and anyone who can already afford them, are left largely untouched.

## Five days, or a real fix
Whether trading volume in these products actually drops once the higher deposit and the August 19 tracking-error rule are both in effect will show whether this was a genuine circuit-breaker on leverage-driven volatility, or mostly a symbolic gesture that raises the entry price without changing who's most exposed.
serenity-amd-helios-cpo-networking:
AMD's networking partners for its next-generation Helios AI server racks expect the company to move to co-packaged optics eventually, according to informal channel checks relayed by investor Serenity on X, though the specifics are worth separating carefully from what AMD has actually confirmed.

## What Helios is, and what it isn't yet
Helios is AMD's first rack-scale AI system, a roughly 7,000-pound cabinet packing 72 of its newest Instinct MI455X GPUs alongside Venice CPUs, built to compete directly with Nvidia's NVL72 racks. Helios itself uses today's standard copper and pluggable-optic connections, not co-packaged optics, or CPO, the technique of building fiber-optic connections directly into a chip's package instead of using separate modules. AMD's own confirmed CPO work is tied to its later MI500 generation, code-named Verona, expected around 2027-28, through a reported silicon-photonics partnership with GlobalFoundries.

@@REF@@AMD reportedly establishes $280 million silicon photonics hub in Taiwan (Tom's Hardware, 2026)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/amd-reportedly-establishes-usd280-million-silicon-photonics-hub-in-taiwan-new-r-and-d-center-could-accelerate-companys-co-packaged-optics-roadmap|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/85Ensc6aXdvm6joZA7UnV3-1600-80.jpg

## The 'no delays' pushback is about a different company's timeline
An unnamed AI infrastructure executive involved in a hyperscaler's CPO supply chain told Serenity there is no sign of the delays some third-party reports have recently flagged. Those delay reports appear to trace to a separate industry debate over Nvidia and Broadcom's switch-side CPO ramp, which one widely circulated analyst note argued could slip into 2027-2029, a claim that has itself been disputed, with other trackers reporting Nvidia's Spectrum-X CPO and Broadcom's Bailly switches already in volume ramp. AMD's Helios and its later CPO roadmap are a separate matter from that specific controversy.

@@REF@@AMD MI455X and Helios: 432GB HBM4, 72-GPU Racks, and a Real Answer to Vera Rubin (StorageReview, 2026)|https://www.storagereview.com/news/amd-mi455x-and-helios-432gb-hbm4-72-gpu-racks-and-a-real-answer-to-vera-rubin|https://www.storagereview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/StorageReview-AMD-Helios-14.jpg

## Why the distinction matters
As AI clusters scale into the tens of thousands of chips, today's copper and pluggable-optic connections become a bottleneck on both power draw and bandwidth, and moving optics onto the chip package is one of the industry's clearest paths to keep scaling without a proportional jump in power use. That is the strategic logic partners are reportedly telling Serenity applies to AMD and the wider hyperscaler industry over time, but it describes a multi-year roadmap starting with Helios's successor, not a claim about what Helios itself ships with today.

## An early signal, not a confirmed one
Serenity flagged the commentary as informal, not official guidance from AMD or its partners. Given it rests on a single anonymous executive and unnamed channel checks, and appears to conflate AMD's own later-stage CPO plans with a separate Nvidia and Broadcom timeline dispute, it is best read as an early, unverified signal about the direction of the industry rather than a confirmed AMD roadmap.
kobeissi-intel-q2-earnings-surge:
Intel's stock jumped more than 11% after its second-quarter results beat Wall Street on almost every line, according to the Kobeissi Letter, as the company's AI data center business drove its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than fifteen years.

## The headline numbers
Revenue came in at $16.13 billion, up 25% year over year and about 12% above the $14.42 billion analysts had expected, with the Data Center and AI segment alone growing 59% to $6.3 billion. On an adjusted basis, Intel posted a $2.2 billion profit, and adjusted earnings per share of $0.42 nearly doubled the $0.22 Wall Street had modeled. CEO Lip-Bu Tan called it the company's strongest quarterly revenue growth in over fifteen years.

@@REF@@Intel Reports Second-Quarter 2026 Financial Results (Intel Newsroom, 2026-07-23)|https://newsroom.intel.com/corporate/intel-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results|https://newsroom.intel.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/intel-card-scaled.jpg

## The $11 billion loss isn't what it sounds like, but it isn't going away either
Under standard accounting rules, Intel still posted an $11 billion GAAP net loss, driven by roughly $12.6 billion in charges. That charge is not a one-off write-down, it comes from marking to market the equity stake the US government took in Intel in 2025 under the CHIPS Act arrangement, which is revalued against Intel's stock price every quarter. That means Intel's GAAP results now move in the opposite direction of its own share price gains for as long as the government holds that stake, a structural quirk rather than a cleanup charge investors can expect to disappear.

@@REF@@Intel reported a huge earnings beat. Analysts are on the fence regarding the chipmaker (CNBC, 2026-07-24)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/24/intel-reported-a-huge-earnings-beat-analysts-remain-on-the-fence-.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108339567-1784842862625-gettyimages-2287372611-_88a2619_7hjlkutv.jpeg?v=1784842934&w=1920&h=1080

## The pop faded fast
Intel guided third-quarter revenue to $15.8 billion to $16.8 billion and an adjusted gross margin of 42%, broadly in line with its current run rate, but also raised full-year 2026 capital spending guidance to more than $20 billion, up from roughly $18 billion. The initial after-hours jump of 12-13% cooled to under 4% by the next morning, and shares fell about 8% the following trading day as investors weighed the bigger capex bill against the revenue beat. Intel's foundry business, still reliant on internal transfers for most of its revenue, remains the weaker half of the story that the Data Center and AI numbers are masking.

## What it says about the AI cycle
The result adds a legacy chipmaker, one many investors had written off in the AI race, to the list of companies, alongside AMD and Nvidia's supply chain, showing that AI infrastructure spending keeps outrunning expectations even as the rest of the economy slows. Whether that justifies Intel's now much larger capex bill is the question the stock's next-day drop suggests the market hasn't settled yet.
trump-saudi-nuclear-abraham-accords:
President Trump said on Truth Social that the newly announced US-Saudi civil nuclear cooperation deal will be approved, but only if Saudi Arabia joins the Abraham Accords, the US-brokered framework normalizing relations between Arab states and Israel.

## A condition added after the ink was dry
The US Department of Energy had announced the deal just a day earlier, on July 22, 2026, describing it as a multi-billion-dollar, decades-long civil nuclear partnership. The Energy Department's own announcement made no mention of Israel or the Abraham Accords. That means Trump's post added the Israel-recognition condition after the deal was already signed, not as part of the original terms, a sequencing Senator Chris Van Hollen publicly called a bait-and-switch.

@@REF@@Trump says Saudi nuclear deal contingent on relations with Israel, does not include enrichment (CNBC, 2026-07-23)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/23/trump-saudi-arabia-nuclear-power.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108338791-1784750900959-gettyimages-2286590112-AFP_C2WF98P.jpeg?v=1784750930&w=1920&h=1080

## Not entirely new, but a reversal
Trump stressed there would be 'no enrichment of material,' meaning Saudi Arabia would receive non-military nuclear technology similar to what Iran and the UAE already have, not the ability to enrich uranium itself. The Abraham Accords linkage itself isn't unprecedented, a version of it was part of the US approach under the prior administration, but Trump had appeared to drop that condition earlier this year before reinstating it in this post.

@@REF@@After nuke deal already signed, Trump insists it's conditioned on Saudi Arabia joining Abraham Accords (The Times of Israel, 2026-07-23)|https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/trump-nuclear-deal-conditioned-on-saudi-arabia-joining-abraham-accords/

## Congress and the IAEA still have a say
Any final US-Saudi nuclear cooperation agreement is a Section 123 agreement under the Atomic Energy Act, meaning it faces a 90-day congressional review period during which lawmakers could vote to block it, subject to a presidential veto. Republican Senator John Kennedy broke with Trump publicly, calling the timing a hair trigger so soon after US strikes on Iran's own nuclear program, while adding he doubts Saudi Arabia will actually join the Accords anyway. Saudi Arabia has so far declined to join, unlike the UAE and Bahrain, and has consistently tied normalization to progress on Palestinian statehood.

## A nuclear deal now doubles as a diplomatic lever
Tying a multi-billion-dollar nuclear energy deal, of direct interest to uranium and nuclear-equipment suppliers eyeing new Gulf reactor demand, to a geopolitical demand raises the stakes for both sides. Either Saudi Arabia makes a move it has resisted for years, or a nuclear partnership that had already been signed stalls over a condition attached after the fact.
kobeissi-10y-yield-breaks-470:
The US 10-Year Treasury yield officially broke above 4.70% on July 23, its highest level since January 2025, according to the Kobeissi Letter, surpassing even the roughly 4.5% high set during last year's tariff-driven Liberation Day selloff in April 2025.

## What's confirmed
CNBC and CNN independently confirmed the 10-Year hit about 4.71% that day, its highest since January 2025, and that the 30-Year yield has spent its longest stretch above 5% since 2007. Both moves put the benchmark that anchors mortgages, corporate borrowing, and the US government's own debt costs on track for a fresh 52-week high.

@@REF@@10-year Treasury yield rises to highest since January 2025 as surging oil rekindles inflation fear (CNBC, 2026-07-23)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/23/treasury-yields-oil-prices-jobless-claims.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/105118559-fem_trader.jpg?v=1710517273&w=1920&h=1080

## More than one story is driving this
The Kobeissi framing credits the Iran war almost entirely, but coverage that same day describes a more layered picture. Oil-driven inflation fear is one thread, alongside markets repricing toward a possible rate hike rather than just fewer cuts, uncertainty around incoming Fed chair Kevin Warsh, and fiscal concerns as war costs add to Treasury issuance. One account went as far as calling the Fed-leadership question probably the biggest single driver.

@@REF@@The world's most important market is flashing red about the Iran war (CNN Business, 2026-07-23)|https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/23/economy/bond-market-inflation-iran|https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/gettyimages-1246358539-20260722154546950.jpg?c=16x9&q=w_800,c_fill

## The Liberation Day comparison holds up numerically
The April 2025 tariff-panic peak was around 4.5%, so July's 4.71% genuinely does surpass it, though no single article in the day's coverage states that comparison directly, it follows from combining the two data points rather than being a claim reporters made themselves.

## Why the mix of causes matters
Rising long-term yields typically raise the discount rate applied to future corporate profits, a headwind that lands hardest on richly valued growth and AI stocks, while also raising Washington's own interest bill on new debt. Whether that pressure eases depends on which driver is actually dominant, an Iran war that could de-escalate, a Fed leadership question that resolves one way or another, or a fiscal supply problem that doesn't go away regardless of the war's outcome.
kobeissi-nasdaq-900b-selloff:
The Kobeissi Letter reported that the S&P 500 wiped out roughly $900 billion in market capitalization on July 23, framing it as the Nasdaq 100 extending its drop past 2.5% on Iran war escalation and tech earnings reactions.

## The number and the cause don't hold up against independent reporting
The S&P 500 actually closed down 1.21% that day, a move that translates to roughly $650-670 billion given the index's total market cap at the time, not $900 billion. The figure independent outlets do verify is different and narrower: Bloomberg reported a $797 billion single-session loss specifically in the Magnificent Seven, the seven largest tech megacaps, not the S&P 500 as a whole.

@@REF@@Magnificent 7 Lose $797 Billion as AI Skeptics Dump Tech Stocks (Bloomberg, 2026-07-23)|https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-23/magnificent-7-loses-767-billion-as-ai-skeptics-dump-tech-stocks

## AI-capex fear, not the Iran war, was the primary driver
Every independent account of that day's selloff, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance, and CNBC among them, points to AI-capex and earnings shock as the main cause: Alphabet fell about 6% on AI infrastructure spending fears and Tesla dropped 14-15% on disappointing earnings and its own AI spending plans. The Iran war and its effect on oil prices are cited across that coverage as a real but secondary, compounding factor, not the headline cause the Kobeissi framing suggests.

@@REF@@Shortsighted stock market can no longer brush off war: 'It's too hard to ignore $100 oil' (CNBC, 2026-07-23)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/23/short-sighted-stock-market-can-no-longer-brush-off-war-investors-say.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108337404-17845637512026-07-20t160708z_1331384416_rc2phmayntj4_rtrmadp_0_usa-stocks.jpeg?v=1784563809&w=1920&h=1080

## The parts of the picture that do check out
The same-day moves in other markets are real: Brent and WTI crude both surged past fresh milestones after Houthi forces struck Saudi oil tankers, and the 10-Year Treasury yield broke above 4.70% for the first time since January 2025. Those two markets were genuinely reacting to the widening Iran war. The mistake is importing that same causal story wholesale into the equity selloff, when the stocks doing the heaviest damage that day were falling on their own earnings news.

## Why the distinction matters
A $797 billion Magnificent Seven selloff driven by AI-capex jitters is a different trade than a $900 billion market-wide selloff driven by war escalation. One says investors are questioning whether AI spending pays off; the other says geopolitical risk is repricing the entire market. Conflating the two, as the original framing does, points traders toward the wrong hedge for what actually happened that day.
kobeissi-brent-oil-100-milestone:
Brent crude has broken back above $100 a barrel, and the Kobeissi Letter says inflation expectations and interest rates are climbing sharply again as a result.

## The move is real, but the pace is a rough estimate
Brent traded around $71.5-$72.4 a barrel in early July before rising to just above $100 by July 23, a move in the ballpark of the roughly 40% the original figure claimed, though no single sourced article pins down an exact '42% in 20 days' statistic, so that number is best treated as an approximation rather than a precise, independently verified figure.

@@REF@@Brent crude crosses $100 after tankers reportedly struck off Saudi Arabia (CNBC, 2026-07-23)|https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/23/oil-prices-today-wti-brent-trump-iran-hormuz.html|https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108334811-1784044841219-2026-07-14T101926Z_1707699432_RC2CI9AZ3FKO_RTRMADP_3_IRAN-CRISIS-SHIPPING-EMIRATES.JPG?v=1784044960&w=1920&h=1080

## This isn't oil's first trip to $100-plus in this war
What the original framing leaves out matters: this same Iran war already sent Brent to $126 a barrel, a four-year high, on April 30, 2026. Prices then fell more than 38% from that peak, dropping below $70 by early July on ceasefire and diplomacy optimism, before this latest escalation reversed the decline. The July move to $100 is the second leg of an ongoing rollercoaster tied to one conflict, not a fresh, first-of-its-kind milestone.

@@REF@@Oil prices fall to levels not seen since start of US-Israel war on Iran (Al Jazeera, 2026-07-02)|https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/7/2/oil-prices-fall-to-levels-not-seen-since-start-of-us-israel-war-on-iran|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2026-07-01T093820Z_1180277915_RC2AWLAKSPWG_RTRMADP_3_IRAN-CRISIS-SHIPPING-FEES-1782963523_758afb-1782968112.jpg?resize=1200%2C630&quality=80

## Why the level still matters
$100 is a psychological line that traders and central banks watch closely, since oil feeds directly into gasoline, shipping, and nearly everything else. This latest leg up builds on a month of escalating headlines, Houthi tanker strikes, Iran threatening energy infrastructure, and warnings that the Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war shipping conditions, each adding its own premium on top of the last.

## The question this history raises
If oil holds near $100, central banks leaning toward cutting rates face a harder case, and fuel-dependent companies face a fresh squeeze. But given that the same war already produced a much larger spike that fully reversed within ten weeks, the more useful question may not be how high oil goes if the war escalates further, but how much of this move survives if diplomacy makes any progress at all.
jukan-ymtc-nand-share-surpasses-micron:
Chinese memory maker YMTC has overtaken both Micron and SanDisk in NAND flash market share, according to unnamed third-party data cited by semiconductor analyst Jukan, closing the gap with fourth-ranked Kioxia to just 0.4 percentage points. That specific claim, however, doesn't line up with what named research firms are actually reporting.

## What named research firms show instead
TrendForce's official Q1 2026 NAND report doesn't rank YMTC among the top five suppliers at all, showing Samsung at 31.6%, SK hynix at 17.6%, and Kioxia, Micron, and SanDisk in a three-way tie at 13.9% each. Counterpoint Research data from around late June 2026 comes closer to Jukan's framing but still describes a tie rather than an overtake, putting Samsung at 29%, SK hynix at 14%, Kioxia at 14%, and YMTC, Micron, and SanDisk together at roughly 13%.

@@REF@@Combined Revenue of Top Five Global NAND Flash Suppliers Rose 83.7% QoQ for 1Q26 (TrendForce, 2026-05-25)|https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260525-13058.html|https://img.trendforce.com/EDM/2026/05/20260525_095916_tf-press-center--2-.jpg

## The growth rate is the real headline
What's well-documented is how fast YMTC got there. Counterpoint puts YMTC's NAND share at just 8% a year earlier, meaning its jump to roughly 13% represents around 445% year-over-year revenue growth, the fastest of any major NAND supplier. YMTC is racing to build two to three new fabs in Wuhan targeting roughly 500,000 wafers a month, using an increasingly domestic equipment supply chain, over 50% by some estimates, to work around US restrictions on advanced lithography and deposition tools, with a stated goal of 15% global NAND share by the end of 2026.

@@REF@@China's YMTC Global NAND Market Share Jumps to 13%, Now Tied With SanDisk (ZeroHedge, citing Counterpoint Research, 2026-06)|https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/chinas-ymtc-global-nand-market-share-jumps-13-tied-sandisk|https://assets.zerohedge.com/s3fs-public/styles/16_9_max_700/public/2026-06/ymtc%20market%20share%201.png?itok=bierjVr9

## Where the pressure actually lands
Analyst commentary frames the competitive threat as concentrated in commodity NAND, where YMTC and its DRAM counterpart CXMT are catching up quickly and pressuring SanDisk specifically, while Micron's larger enterprise and HBM-adjacent product mix is seen as somewhat more insulated. Both Micron and SanDisk have leaned on tight NAND supply and AI-driven demand to defend pricing this year, and a Chinese competitor at parity narrows the room to raise prices further.

## Reading the claim correctly
Jukan's own figures, the overtake and the 0.4-point gap to Kioxia, trace to unnamed third-party data rather than a named research firm, and should be read as his source's specific claim rather than an independently confirmed ranking. The verified baseline, a three-way tie built on the fastest growth rate in the industry, is arguably the more durable story regardless of whose count is most precise.

jukan-intel-amd-china-cpu-lta:
Intel and AMD are negotiating long-term supply agreements with major Chinese server customers, according to a Reuters report relayed by semiconductor analyst Jukan on X, responding to a real and well-documented price squeeze.

## The deal structure and the numbers behind it
The agreements span roughly one to more than two years, locking in purchase volumes while letting prices float with the market, meaning buyers guarantee volume but stay exposed to further price increases rather than getting a fixed price. Server CPU prices in China have risen more than 40% since the start of 2026, with some months seeing increases of over 10%, consistently reported across Reuters, Tom's Hardware, and other outlets covering the story.

@@REF@@Intel and AMD sign long-term server CPU deals with Chinese customers as prices jump over 40% (Tom's Hardware, 2026-07-23)|https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/cpus/intel-and-amd-sign-long-term-server-cpu-deals-with-chinese-customers-as-prices-jump-over-40-percent|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cAk7qELwnmUnwAMSKkDXw3-2000-80.jpg

## The six-month lead time figure needs a date stamp
The claim that some Intel lead times stretched to six months originates from a Reuters and Tom's Hardware report in February 2026; by March, industry coverage described lead times more conservatively as roughly 8 to 12 weeks. The six-month figure is real but reflects an earlier snapshot within this story, not necessarily the situation as of the July agreements.

@@REF@@Intel, AMD server CPUs reportedly suffering from supply shortages in China (Tom's Hardware, 2026-02-06)|https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/cpus/intel-amd-server-cpus-reportedly-suffering-from-supply-shortages-in-china-leading-to-increased-prices-sources-say-orders-could-be-delayed-by-as-much-as-6-months|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VBnZto6P3Yzh9RfNDACjGT-2560-80.jpg

## Why China specifically
Server CPUs, unlike GPUs, are not covered by US export controls, making them one of the few AI-infrastructure components Chinese buyers can still purchase freely. That funnels demand toward Intel and AMD even as a broader AI-driven chip and memory shortage pulls fab capacity toward other products, compounded by reports of buyers stockpiling ahead of any further restrictions.

## A pattern, or one investor's framing of several separate stories
Investor Serenity placed the CPU deals inside a wider narrative: long-term agreements spreading in 2026 from memory chips, where Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix signed multi-year DRAM and NAND deals, into photonics components, and now into CPUs and reportedly passive parts like MLCCs. Each of those individual shortages is separately documented, but no outlet ties them together as one unified industry-wide trend the way Serenity's framing does, so that synthesis is best read as her own interpretation rather than an established fact.
jukan-deepseek-huawei-cuda-moat:
Semiconductor analyst Jukan says he has turned very bearish on Nvidia, and the trigger is a reportedly leaked investor call from DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng. The point is simple. What has really protected Nvidia is not chip speed but software, and AI coding tools are tearing that wall down fast.
One thing to nail down first. Wenfeng's remarks come from a private call that was reportedly leaked. Neither he nor DeepSeek has confirmed them.

## The wall isn't the chip?
CUDA is the software layer that lets developers run AI programs on Nvidia chips.
It launched in 2006 and has built up for nearly two decades. Nvidia counts six million developers on it and more than 150 libraries.
The catch is that years of written code are tied to those libraries. Moving to a rival's chip means rewriting all of it, and that switching cost is the moat.
A slightly faster chip means nothing if the software can't come with it.

## How did DeepSeek get around it?
When DeepSeek trained its V3 model, it already skipped CUDA for some tasks and wrote PTX directly.
PTX sits one level below CUDA, closer to the chip. It takes more work but leans less on Nvidia's software.
Then came TileLang, an open-source tool built by a Peking University group with Microsoft Research support. It re-emits the same code for different chips.
If those tools are quickly fitted to Huawei chips with AI coding assistants, Wenfeng argues, the software gap for Chinese chips largely disappears within a year.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|An Nvidia GPU board. What guarded this chip was never just performance, but the software that runs on top of it.|Wikimedia Commons|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

@@REF@@DeepSeek bypasses industry-standard CUDA, uses assembly-like PTX instead (Tom's Hardware, 2025-01-28)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/deepseeks-ai-breakthrough-bypasses-industry-standard-cuda-uses-assembly-like-ptx-programming-instead|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Wb8pUe4iWjBf2Gx8ky5rLA-2560-80.jpg

## Do those tools actually exist?
They are not just talk. You can find the published code.

@@CHK@@TileLang|MIT open source|Huawei Ascend backend|tilelang-ascend is real|DeepSeek kernel repo|TileKernels published@@The premise of Wenfeng's claim, that the tools can move to Huawei chips, is backed by code that is actually public. But this only means the porting path exists, not that the hardware efficiency gap has closed.@@Checked 2026-07-27 · GitHub tile-ai/tilelang · tile-ai/tilelang-ascend · deepseek-ai/TileKernels

Huawei is already shipping chips for that software to run on: the Ascend 950 line and the Atlas 950 SuperPoD that bundles them.
But every "several times Nvidia" figure Huawei points to is its own claim. No independent benchmark has verified it yet.

@@REF@@Huawei, DeepSeek strengthen China's AI self-reliance with V4 collaboration (SCMP, 2026-04-24)|https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3351349/huawei-deepseek-strengthen-chinas-ai-self-reliance-collaboration-v4-model|https://cdn.i-scmp.com/sites/default/files/styles/og_image_scmp_generic/public/d8/images/canvas/2026/04/24/6418f316-a9dc-438c-86c5-c3b825d95a11_693e3e8a.jpg?itok=rKQJIuY4&v=1777030291

## So how big is the gap?
Here the readings split head-on.

@@CMP@@CFR's reading|The hardware gap is about 5x today and widens to 17x by 2027 (Dec 2025 report).|Wenfeng's reading (leaked, unverified)|Just 4x per chip and two years, and once the software moves, even that is the only bottleneck left.

One side sees the same gap widening, the other sees it as narrow. Jukan's bearish case leans on the second, and the fact that the second rests on an unverified leak does not go away.

## Is AMD the same story?
Jukan extends the logic into a bull case for AMD.
AMD has ROCm, its own answer to CUDA. It is open source, started in 2016, and even in last week's release AMD writes that it is still closing the gap.
The same AI coding tools could speed that work up, and AMD happens to be investing in Anthropic and using Claude Code for its own chip design.
If the software wall really is getting lower, the benefit goes not only to Huawei but to AMD.
kobeissi-houthi-tanker-strike: Brent crude jumped above $98 a barrel after Yemen's Houthi forces struck two Saudi Arabian oil tankers, according to the Kobeissi Letter, and within hours US crude followed, trading above $90 a barrel for the first time since June 11. The Houthis, an Iran-aligned armed group that controls much of Yemen and has repeatedly targeted shipping in the Red Sea and nearby waters, striking Saudi tankers directly widens the conflict beyond the Hormuz chokepoint that has dominated headlines so far, giving traders a second geography to watch. semianalysis-vera-rubin-nvl72-tco: Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin NVL72 rack system is delivering roughly five times the performance per dollar and 5.4 times the performance per megawatt of today's Blackwell GB200 NVL72, according to early benchmark data reviewed by semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis. The numbers come from engineering samples run on the AI model DeepSeek R1, and the gap widens further when compared against GB200's own rough early bringup period in 2025, since Rubin is still in that same early stage now and its results are expected to keep improving as the surrounding software matures, the same pattern SemiAnalysis says it saw with Blackwell. The early figures were gathered by cloud provider CoreWeave and have not been independently verified. Nvidia has committed to submitting checkable numbers to the industry benchmark group InferenceX by the third quarter of 2026, with Google expected to submit results for its TPUv7 chip and AMD for its MI455X chip around the same time, which would let investors compare all three on equal footing for the first time. One reason SemiAnalysis expects a smoother rollout for Rubin is software continuity, its chip can reuse Blackwell's low-level code, unlike Blackwell, which could not reuse the prior generation's, a technical detail that can determine how quickly a new chip generation actually reaches full performance in production.
jukan-samsung-elec-mechanics-mlcc-lta: Samsung Electro-Mechanics has signed a long-term supply agreement for MLCCs, the tiny ceramic capacitors used in nearly every electronic device, with a customer it identified only as 'a large global company', according to a post from semiconductor analyst Jukan on X. Jukan's read is that the vague description points to a major technology company, and that the significance is less about this one deal and more about the pattern it confirms, that long-term agreements, the multi-year contracts that lock in supply and pricing years in advance, are spreading beyond memory chips into passive components like MLCCs. That pattern has already reshaped the memory chip market this year, where SK hynix and Samsung Electronics have used LTAs to guarantee revenue from AI-hungry customers regardless of the usual boom-bust cycle. If the same dynamic is now taking hold for a component as basic and previously commoditized as MLCCs, Jukan suggests it is a sign that Big Tech's appetite for guaranteed component supply is broadening well past the chips that get the most attention, toward the more ordinary parts that go into every server and device.
kobeissi-china-star50-record-inflow: Chinese investors poured a record $2.0 billion into the Star 50 ETF, the country's largest tech-focused fund, on a single day this week, according to the Kobeissi Letter, more than double the previous daily record set in December 2020. The rebound follows a rough stretch just last week, when a wave of forced selling wiped out roughly $37 billion in margin debt over four days as leveraged bets on chip stocks unwound, dragging the same index down sharply. The comeback has state-linked money behind it too. China's so-called National Team funds, state-backed investment vehicles that typically step in to support markets during selloffs, took in $10 billion over the last three trading sessions, the most since April 2025. Separately, at least five of China's largest insurers have pledged to increase their stock holdings, with one insurer, China Life, alone buying more than $1.5 billion of stocks and funds. Kobeissi's read is straightforward, Chinese investors keep showing up to buy dips, turning what looked like a leverage-driven crash into a fast, well-supported recovery.
meru-googl-q2-results-korea-impact: Alphabet raised its 2026 capital spending guidance to $195 billion-$205 billion, up from $180 billion-$190 billion, even as free cash flow swung negative for the first time, the Korean blogger Meru writes in a same-day breakdown of the earnings call. First-half capex now totals $80.6 billion, $35.7 billion in Q1 plus $44.9 billion in Q2, meaning the second half needs $57.2 billion to $62.2 billion per quarter to hit the new guidance, more than the first half's pace. On the earnings call, Google's CFO said the company plans to lease more third-party computing capacity in the third quarter as a bridge while it builds out its own data centers, and reiterated that Google remains compute constrained with very strong AI demand. Cloud order backlog grew from $462 billion in Q1 to $514 billion in Q2, an 11.3 percent rise Meru calls solid evidence that memory demand keeps building, though he notes bulls will call the record backlog reassuring while bears will call the 11 percent sequential growth a slowdown from the prior quarter's near-doubling. The catch is cash, operating cash flow of $39.1 billion minus $44.9 billion of capex left free cash flow at negative $5.8 billion, down $11.2 billion from a year earlier. camillo-googl-earnings-noise: Chris Camillo, the trader known for pioneering social arbitrage, a strategy of spotting stock ideas by tracking everyday consumer trends and social media chatter before Wall Street catches on, says investors who panicked over Google parent Alphabet's stock swings right after its latest earnings were reacting, not thinking. He calls it comical that so much of financial commentary on X melted down within minutes of the earnings release, arguing that the right response to sharp, AI-driven market swings is to regulate your own reaction rather than mirror the market's mood. Camillo, who also co-founded the consumer-trend research firm TickerTags and wrote the investing book Laughing at Wall Street, argues that 2026's market has become one of the most manic and confused he's seen, largely because AI is reshaping how investors price growth and risk in real time. His conclusion is that investors willing to do the research, hold a strong conviction, and sit through short-term noise are the ones likely to be rewarded over the long run, a philosophy that runs through his social arbitrage approach to picking stocks well before they become obvious.

serenity-googl-q2-cloud-beat: Alphabet's second-quarter results blew past Wall Street's estimates and the company raised its already enormous 2026 capital spending plan, according to a rundown from the X account Serenity. kobeissi-iran-eye-for-eye-warning: Two of Iran's most senior officials used near identical language within about 25 minutes of each other on July 22, both signaling that Tehran will not de-escalate and that infrastructure on either side is now fair game. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war conditions, warning that if a region does not sell oil, no one will sell oil, and that no infrastructure will be safe unless Iran's security is guaranteed. Shortly after, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described Iran's defense doctrine as an eye for an eye, saying any aggression against Iranian infrastructure would draw a powerful and decisive response, and that anyone who supports such aggression, in whatever form, would also be treated as a legitimate target. The statements arrived hours after President Trump posted that the United States would destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant every time Iran fired on a ship in the Strait, and after Iran's own warning that it would target energy sites if the US bombs its power plants. Rather than walking anything back, two separate branches of Iran's government used the same day to restate the threat in even blunter terms, explicitly widening the list of legitimate targets to include third parties that provide support. The overlapping statements from Iran's diplomatic and legislative leadership suggest the retaliation rhetoric is becoming official policy rather than a single official's talking point, keeping the risk of escalation around Hormuz elevated.
